records.name: ASAP Chess
records.summary: ASAP (After School Activities Partnerships) runs chess for kids and teens across the city: weekly after-school clubs at schools and libraries, a school chess league, and free Saturday tournaments open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Young players join a weekly club near them, play rated tournaments on Saturdays, or take part in the school league. The program also runs a free summer camp for girls.

schedule.text: Free Saturday tournaments run monthly from October to May. After-school clubs meet weekly, with times set by each club.

locations.label: Citywide, at schools, libraries and rec centers

cost.text: Saturday tournaments are free. Club and league costs are not stated.

first_step.how: Email chess@phillyasap.org, or use the program locator on the ASAP site to find a club near you.
first_step.basis: The chess page lists beginner, intermediate and advanced tournament sections and gives a contact for joining.

records.notes: Homepage tournament dates (Nov 07 and Dec 05) show no year, so the status is probably_active, not active. Age limits and club costs are not stated. The phone number is the general line on the homepage. The only dated source found is a 2019 US Chess article that names ASAP chess.

records.name: Rittenhouse Chess Club
records.summary: Chess players who meet in Rittenhouse Square on Wednesdays and Sundays. The club began when passersby joined informal games, and it also runs tournaments, including a recent charity blitz event.
records.what_you_do: Play chess outdoors in the square, or enter the club's tournaments, which draw players from across the city.

schedule.text: Meets Wednesdays and Sundays in Rittenhouse Square, according to a June 2026 news article. Times are not stated.

first_step.how: Go to Rittenhouse Square on a Wednesday or Sunday and join a game. No sign-up or contact was found.
first_step.basis: Passersby joined the informal games, so you can just show up, but no sign-up or contact is published.

records.notes: No club website, email or phone was found. Found in a June 2026 Inquirer article about a charity blitz tournament, and named in a June 2026 Inquirer photo essay. Times and cost are not stated, so check before relying on the schedule.

notes: Searches: 3 of 3 used (cap reached). Fetches: 17. Covered: chess (ASAP, Rittenhouse, and clubs named in a 2019 US Chess article and a 2026 Inquirer photo essay), Go (Penn group only), Scrabble (NASPA roster), and bridge (ACBL pages blocked, so no readable Philadelphia list). NOT covered, because the search budget was spent on chess, bridge and Go: mahjong groups, puzzle hunts, nonprofit trivia leagues, and tabletop or role playing groups in public places. These need a later wave with searches. Skipped on purpose: Queen and Rook Game Cafe (a business in Headhouse Square, where the charity event and some Go sessions were held), Clark Park casual chess (a place, not a group), Vaux and Masterman school chess teams (school teams named in a 2019 article, no current page found), and the Liberty Bell Open and other tournaments (one-time events). Millersville University Go Club is in Lancaster County, out of area. The Penn Clubs page for Penn Go Society returned not found. Most named groups in this slice have no readable own website, which is why only two records were written.
